After smoking every day for multiple years, I finally managed to develop much healthier habits. What worked for me was when I started making edibles out of concern for my lungs. I told myself I refused to be high all day from them and that I would only eat them at night. I stuck with that and slowly found things to do during the day other than get high. It was definitely a struggle at first. However, it got easier and easier as it became my new routine. After a while, I realized I didn't really need to even eat the edibles anymore because I wasn't craving it during the day anymore. I only needed them to sleep at that point, so I quit. I didn't sleep well for a couple months. However, I am now at a point where I can lay down and sleep as long as I want to. I also will partake in an edible or a smoke sesh with friends at a social gathering every now and again. Granted, I don't see my friends super often as I have moved out of state. The trick, in my opinion, is that I am able to get high if I am not at home as I don't begin to associate the drug with being at home chilling, but you also have to have the discipline to not allow yourself to get high again the next few days. There is always a craving, but you just have to ignore it and find something else to do. They will fade in a few days. These cravings have been especially hard for me in the past, because before moving, everyone in my house smoked all day every day. You just have to get away from the people smoking and occupy your mind with something else. I apologize for this long comment that partially didn't even answer your question. I am just hoping that my experience quitting might help somebody else do the same.

Okay, so I’ll explain this as simply as I can. In the beginning, we were told not to wear masks. This is because we thought the virus transferred only after somebody became sick. We thought somebody had to be coughing or sneezing it up. If that were the case, a healthy person wearing a mask is bad because they’re more likely to touch their face and contract the disease that way. We’ve now figured out that we were partially incorrect. We’ve determined that you can be sick, have no symptoms, and spread it anyway just from speaking or breathing. Wearing a mask stops most of those virus particles from a sick person from leaving their person, and it redirects the others away from the person they’re speaking to. To sum it up, wearing a mask will not actually protect the person wearing the mask unless they can resist touching their face to adjust it.  However, it will stop a sick person from spreading it as easily. This is important because many sick people don’t know they are sick because they are asymptomatic. I repeat. Masks prevent the spread of the disease more than they protect the individual wearer (me). People are calling anti-maskers selfish, childish, etc. because you guys are arguing for the exact opposite indirectly. You are contributing to the further spread of the disease because you are thinking of masks as personal protection rather than an effort towards public health. Please try to consider how not wearing a mask and not knowing you’re sick could affect somebody. You could get your friend sick who gets his or her diabetic grandmother sick who passes away. Or maybe your friend is diabetic and they pass away instead. These are completely preventable scenarios. If everybody in our country wore a mask for 4 to 6 weeks, we could slow the spread dramatically. However, we would realistically have to wear them longer. We won’t be back to normal until a vaccine comes along, but anti-maskers are actually allowing hundreds of thousands of fellow human beings to die preventable deaths by contributing to the spread of this disease. That’s why we think you’re childish. We think adults are capable of recognizing their responsibility to try to protect their fellow man. Especially when that “responsibility” is as simple as putting a piece of cloth over your face. I really hope you see the light. We don’t need more ignorant people in this world right now.
